research_question: Can articulation structure be mathematically linked to continuation geometry within the bounded Notebook 12/13/14 domain, rather than treated only as a predictive feature?
hypothesis: Articulation hierarchy is not merely feature importance; within the bounded continuation-graph domain it marks structural separation constraints that may be expressible as theorem candidates, falsifiable implications, or counterexample classes relating obstruction, partial reconvergence, and universal reconvergence.

independent_variables.name: articulation_structure
independent_variables.definition: Articulation point count, articulation depth range, hierarchy profile, and induced component splits in the continuation graph.
independent_variables.allowed_values_or_range: Values recoverable from Notebook 13 v2 invariant table and, where graph reconstruction is available, induced articulation substructures.

independent_variables.name: theorem_candidate
independent_variables.definition: A formally stated implication or equivalence candidate connecting articulation structure to continuation geometry.
independent_variables.allowed_values_or_range: Necessary condition, sufficient condition, biconditional, limitation, or counterexample class.

dependent_variables.name: theorem_candidate_status
dependent_variables.definition: Observed status of each articulation theorem candidate inside the bounded domain.

dependent_variables.name: counterexample_count
dependent_variables.definition: Number of rows or reconstructed graphs refuting the candidate condition.

controls.name: no_ml_primary_method
controls.purpose: Stop treating the question as a predictive classification problem.
controls.implementation: Do not use classifier accuracy as the primary output; use implication tables, proof-obligation tables, and counterexample catalogs.

controls.name: counterexample_first
controls.purpose: Prevent theorem escalation from pattern matching.
controls.implementation: Every candidate theorem must report explicit counterexample counts and example config IDs.

controls.name: claim_ceiling_guard
controls.purpose: Prevent C2 observations from being promoted into formal theorem status.
controls.implementation: All theorem candidates remain C1/C2 candidate statements until formal proof work is added under the mathematics additive-only rule.

controls.name: causal_language_guard
controls.purpose: Distinguish causal articulation claims from structural consequence claims.
controls.implementation: Each candidate must be classified as causal_candidate, consequence_candidate, equivalence_candidate, or unresolved_directionality.

random_seed.seed_scope: Only deterministic sampling for examples if a table is too large to display.
random_seed.derivation_policy: Fixed before execution; no stochastic classifier is part of the primary method.

parameter_space.name: notebook_13_v2_invariant_domain
parameter_space.values_or_range: All rows in topological_invariants.parquet from the registered Notebook 13 v2 result archive.
parameter_space.sampling_rule: Use all rows for implication/counterexample tables.

parameter_space.name: notebook_14_ablation_context
parameter_space.values_or_range: Notebook 14 result review showing articulation-hierarchy removal produced the largest single-family accuracy drop.
parameter_space.sampling_rule: Use as motivation only, not as proof.

termination_conditions: All declared theorem candidates are evaluated against the available invariant table.
Each candidate has a status, counterexample count, and example config IDs when refuted.
A proof-obligation table is written for candidates not refuted in the bounded domain.
No formal theorem status is assigned without additive mathematics registry work.

expected_outputs.name: articulation_theorem_candidate_table
expected_outputs.interpretation_role: Primary table of articulation-geometry implications and counterexamples.

expected_outputs.name: articulation_counterexample_catalog
expected_outputs.interpretation_role: Recoverable counterexample catalog for failed theorem candidates.

expected_outputs.name: proof_obligation_table
expected_outputs.interpretation_role: Lists exact definitions and proof obligations required before theorem promotion.

expected_outputs.name: output_manifest
expected_outputs.interpretation_role: Binds source archives, outputs, claim ceiling, and non-claim constraints.

decision_rules: SUPPORTED_C2_CANDIDATE: a candidate implication has zero counterexamples in the bounded domain and clear proof obligations.
REFUTED_C2_LIMITATION: a candidate implication has one or more counterexamples and must be weakened or discarded.
DIRECTIONALITY_UNRESOLVED: articulation correlates structurally but causal/consequence direction cannot be assigned.
FORMALIZATION_READY: a zero-counterexample candidate has precise definitions and can be routed to mathematics as additive proof work, still without theorem status.
allowed_interpretations: Bounded structural evidence about articulation and continuation geometry.
Theorem-candidate generation for later formal mathematics work.
blocked_interpretations: Formal theorem claim from notebook evidence alone.
Causal articulation claim without independent intervention or proof.
Implementation-independent theory claim before formal proof and approved-tool replication.

immutability.supersession_policy: Do not edit after execution starts; create a new spec_id and link the superseding specification.
